{"claims":[{"claim_text":"On October 20, the government of Lagos State ordered a curfew and the Nigerian military attacked protestors at the Lekki toll gate, killing at least a dozen, according to Amnesty International.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Riot police have been deployed throughout Nigeria since the uprising began, killing at least 56 people over the past two weeks.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) stands in solidarity with Nigeria’s #EndSARS/#EndSwat movement and the rights of Nigerians to protest without being attacked by police or military.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Waves of protest have spread over much of the world since last year, including against white supremacist police violence in the United States and other countries.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The #EndSARS protest wave originates in Nigeria’s vibrant history of social movements and popular mobilizations against unemployment, austerity, oppression and exploitation.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. government has provided long-standing military aid and historic partnerships with Nigerian regimes.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. government’s partnerships with Nigerian regimes include the current so-called “anti-terror” campaign waged by the Buhari government on Boko Haram and the people of northern Nigeria.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The uprising in Nigeria is part of a universal struggle against state violence carried out by exploitative ruling classes.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
